notes:
Inbound from small devtools startup building a cloud-native code assistant. Self-serve signup on 2026-02-25, used free credits, started hitting rate limits during integration. Wants a hosted API path (fast time-to-value) but needs clear info on burst limits and predictable per-minute QPS. Primary asks: long context window (they reference 64k-128k tokens for multi-file repo context), streaming partial tokens for editor latency, typed JS/TS SDK with streaming examples, and low-latency completions for inline editing (target ~150-300ms per token in typical editor flows).

Recent convo highlights: 
- "We need the model to see whole repo diffs + open files — 100k+ context would be ideal." — CTO
- Concerned about cost: "If tokens blow up on long context we need guidance on caching and prefix trimming."
- Wants deterministic completions for code transforms — will evaluate n-best reranking and temperature controls.

Technical details / requirements (user-provided):
- Workloads: inline code completion, multi-file reasoning (analysis+refactor), repo-level search via embeddings.
- Latency SLOs: interactive editor flows ~150-300ms; batch refactor jobs can be slower.
- Throughput: ~200-600 requests/min at current beta, expects 2-3x growth if tight latency.
- Context window desired: 64k tokens preferred, 100k optimistic.
- SDKs: strong ask for typed TypeScript + Node streaming examples, Python asyncio examples; small sample showing incremental token patches for editor integration.
- Streaming: client needs chunked/partial result delivery and ability to cancel and resume.
- Caching: prefix caching looks attractive to cut token costs on repeated repo prompts.

What we did so far:
- 2026-02-25: Self-serve signup, ran basic completions using free credits.
- 2026-03-02: Email to sales about rate limit error during integration (thread attached).
- 2026-03-05: 20m intro call (AE: Elena Park) — demo of fullstack editor flow, walked through sample prompt strategy.
- 2026-03-09: Submitted security questionnaire (requested SOC2 evidence).
- 2026-03-10: Booked follow-up 30m tech call with SE (Jonas Meyer) to discuss streaming and quantization options.

POC ask / success criteria:
- Proof they can hit editor latency target with hosted API under a simulated repo workload (we should provide a small benchmark harness and sample dataset).
- Example SDK snippets for streaming + cancel semantics integrated into their Electron-based editor.
- Pricing guidance for expected token consumption at 64k contexts and best practices for caching/rollups.

Stated blockers: short-term: rate-limit bump during integration; medium-term: internal budget approval.

Sales notes / tone: informal, engineer-centric. Often shorthand. Customer values low-friction onboarding and clear examples. Prioritize technical follow-up over long decks.

Suggested materials to send: 1) Hosted API rate-limit & burst policy doc + request for temporary dev lift, 2) sample TypeScript streaming SDK repo (small), 3) concise one-pager on cost controls (prefix caching, summarization, chunking), 4) SOC2 evidence link.
